title: broaden the compaction seam into a full runtime-host/session-runner lifecycle
description:
# why

zi already has the start of a compaction lifecycle seam, but the post-refactor owner is not a monolithic `SessionController` anymore.

in current zi, the concrete owner chain is:
- `AgentRequest` / request queue for cross-thread mutation requests
- `Interactive` for request dispatch on the agent thread
- `RuntimeHost` for replaceable-session wiring and event bridging
- `SessionRunner` for retry/compaction lifecycle state
- `CompactionExecutor` for concrete compaction execution

overflow recovery already uses that seam. the product now needs it broadened into the full compaction lifecycle contract.

# lifecycle doctrine

a single session-layer owner path must own:
- when compaction is considered
- the reason for compaction (`manual`, `threshold`, `overflow`, pre-prompt policy)
- whether retry follows
- how compaction outcomes interact with live session state refresh
- how session-level events expose compaction semantics

`RuntimeHost` may remain the public facade, but `SessionRunner` is the lifecycle state machine that should own the policy matrix.

# current gap

already landed:
- overflow compaction is a bounded recovery path, not generic transient retry
- runtime tests prove one compact-and-retry pass before continue

still missing:
- a shared lifecycle for manual, threshold, overflow, and pre-prompt compaction
- `compaction_start` parity alongside `compaction_end`
- one authoritative place where compaction reasons and outcomes are composed with retries and prompt submission

# pi-mono lessons to preserve

from `.references/pi-mono/packages/coding-agent/src/core/agent-session.ts`:
- manual compaction is a first-class product flow
- overflow compaction is a bounded recovery path, not generic transient retry
- threshold compaction is a distinct policy from overflow recovery
- pre-prompt compaction checks matter because they catch oversized/aborted contexts before the next send
- session/runtime code, not tui code, decides these policies

# boundaries

this issue is about lifecycle and event semantics, not ui rendering or provider quirks.

it must preserve:
- no tui knowledge in the lifecycle owner
- no provider-specific compaction code
- no compaction policy hidden in ad hoc call sites spread across the app
- one authoritative session-layer place where compaction reasons and outcomes are composed with retries/prompt submission

# acceptance criteria

1. zi has a single session-layer lifecycle contract for compaction reasons and outcomes.
2. manual, threshold, overflow, and pre-prompt paths are modeled as related policies, not disconnected implementations.
3. retry remains distinct from compaction even when the two are composed for overflow recovery.
4. compaction lifecycle semantics are observable without depending on raw agent events or tui internals.
5. issue and code terminology name the real post-refactor owners (`RuntimeHost` / `SessionRunner`) rather than the dead controller shape.
close_reason: runtime-host/session-runner lifecycle exposes compaction_start and compaction_end for overflow/threshold/manual compaction paths; added runtime boundary coverage for start/end ordering; validated zig build, zig fmt --check, zig build test, final zig build, git diff --check

title: manual compaction must cross the request/event boundary
description:
# why

manual compaction is the user-visible entry point that proves whether zi respects its ownership doctrine when a session mutation is initiated from the tui.

right now `/compact` is registered, but it is still a stub. there is no `AgentRequest.compact` variant, so the manual flow does not cross the owner boundary at all.

# boundary doctrine

manual compaction must:
- enter from the tui as an `AgentRequest`
- execute on the agent-owned/session-owned side of the mailbox boundary
- return results and status through `UiEvent` / semantic snapshots
- share the same session-layer lifecycle semantics as auto-compaction, differing only by reason and user initiation

# concrete path to land

`/compact` should become:

```text
slash command
  -> AgentRequest.compact
  -> Interactive.processAgentRequests()
  -> RuntimeHost.runCompaction(.manual, false)
  -> SessionRunner lifecycle events
  -> UiEvent / snapshot publication back to the tui
```

# non-negotiable ownership rules

per `docs/runtime.md`:
- tui never mutates `ca.session_store` or `ca.agent.state` directly
- queue payloads and their backing storage use `msg_allocator`
- no borrowed slices cross the queue
- tui consumes publications; it does not reach back into agent-owned state for compaction internals

# acceptance criteria

1. manual compaction is modeled as a cross-thread mutation request, not a ui shortcut.
2. the manual path reuses the session-layer compaction lifecycle instead of introducing a private side channel.
3. the tui remains a consumer of outcomes and snapshots, not a co-owner of compaction state.
4. manual compaction preserves the existing runtime ownership doctrine without exceptions.
close_reason: manual compaction now enters as AgentRequest.compact, is drained on the agent thread, runs RuntimeHost.runCompaction(.manual), and publishes lifecycle UI/status/conversation events without tui-owned session mutation; validated current tree with zig build, zig fmt --check, zig build test, final zig build, git diff --check

title: define threshold and pre-prompt auto-compaction policy
description:
# why

a usable harness needs more than overflow recovery. pi-mono treats threshold and pre-prompt compaction as first-class product behavior.

without those policies, zi stays reactive and fragile instead of managing long-running sessions predictably.

# current state

current zi already has:
- overflow compact-and-retry in `SessionRunner`
- context-usage tracking that knows usage is unknown immediately after compaction until a post-compaction assistant response lands

current zi still lacks:
- explicit threshold compaction after a turn
- pre-prompt compaction before sending a new prompt
- lifecycle reuse so these policies share the same owner path as overflow and manual compaction

# product policy to preserve

this issue defines the missing auto-compaction policy surface:
- **threshold compaction** after a turn when context crosses the policy threshold, without pretending it is a retry path
- **pre-prompt compaction** before sending a new prompt, so oversized or aborted contexts can be compacted before the next request

# architectural doctrine

these policies must:
- reuse the same compaction lifecycle contract as overflow and manual compaction
- remain model-aware and branch-aware at the session layer
- avoid stale reasoning about context state across compaction boundaries
- preserve the distinction between "compact now" and "compact then automatically retry"

# pi-mono lessons to preserve

from `.references/pi-mono/packages/coding-agent/src/core/agent-session.ts`:
- overflow is one compaction reason, not the only one
- threshold and pre-prompt checks are product behaviors with separate semantics
- model/compaction-boundary awareness matters so stale pre-compaction messages do not retrigger the wrong policy

# acceptance criteria

1. zi has explicit threshold and pre-prompt compaction policies at the session/runtime layer.
2. these policies do not create new side channels outside the established compaction lifecycle.
3. threshold compaction remains distinct from bounded overflow compact-and-retry.
4. the design explicitly accounts for compaction boundaries and model changes at the architecture level.
close_reason: threshold and pre-prompt compaction policies run through SessionRunner/RuntimeHost lifecycle; added pre-prompt boundary coverage and existing post-turn coverage remains green; validated zig build, zig fmt --check, zig build test, final zig build, git diff --check

title: define the extension seam for compaction hooks and artifacts
description:
# why

compaction is part of the product surface. if zi wants extensions to participate later without architectural churn, the compaction seam must be explicit now.

zi already has partial groundwork in the wire format:
- `CompactionEntry.details`
- `CompactionEntry.from_hook`
- `BranchSummaryEntry.details`
- `BranchSummaryEntry.from_hook`

what is still missing is hook plumbing and canonical persistence through the runtime path.

# extension doctrine

compaction extensions must operate through stable, session-layer hook contracts rather than reaching into random internals.

the seam should allow extensions to:
- observe compaction preparation
- cancel compaction
- provide alternate compaction content
- observe the persisted compaction result

while preserving core ownership rules:
- session state remains agent/session owned
- tui does not become the extension bridge for compaction
- persisted `details` / `fromHook` remain explicit and durable

# pi-mono lessons to preserve

from pi-mono's compaction/session hooks:
- `session_before_compact` is a real mutable hook point
- `session_compact` is a real observer hook point
- extension-provided compaction results still flow through the canonical session persistence/rebuild path

# acceptance criteria

1. zi defines a stable compaction hook contract at the session layer.
2. extension-provided compaction still preserves canonical persistence and rebuild semantics.
3. hook payloads are product-grade and future-stable rather than inferred from implementation details.
4. the extension seam does not weaken ownership or thread doctrine.
close_reason: session-layer compaction hook seam is defined in compaction_hooks.zig, registered through AgentSession.setCompactionHooks, and compactor.zig routes proceed/cancel/provide/after hooks through canonical persistence with details/fromHook preserved; validated current tree with zig build, zig fmt --check, zig build test, final zig build, git diff --check

title: kitty protocol negotiation: query response + enable + fallback
description:
root cause of shift+enter not working: kitty protocol is never activated.

zi sends the query (CSI ? u) but never intercepts the response or calls enableKittyProtocol(). the parser (parseKey) correctly handles CSI u format when kitty_active=true, but kitty_active is always false.

fix: implement the negotiation lifecycle:
1. send query CSI ? u
2. intercept response CSI ? <flags> u in raw input
3. if matched → send CSI > 7 u (enable all flags), set kitty_active=true
4. timeout (~150ms) → fall back to xterm modifyOtherKeys mode 2
5. on exit → send CSI < u to pop

also need:
- filter release events (event type 3) when kitty active
- map functional codepoints 57399-57426 (zi-4r0)

references:
- spec: https://sw.kovidgoyal.net/kitty/keyboard-protocol/
- pi-mono: .references/pi-mono/packages/tui/src/terminal.ts:127-193
- ghostty: src/terminal/kitty/key.zig (flag stack model)

title: zig build test hangs on server protocol deadlock (ziglang/zig#15091)
description:
## symptom

`zig build test` hangs indefinitely. direct run of the test binary (`.zig-cache/o/<hash>/test`) completes all 342 tests in ~30s without issue.

## stack traces (taken while hung)

```
test pid: main → test_runner.mainServer → Server.receiveMessage
           → Reader.fill → posix.readv  (blocked on stdin)

build pid: main → runStepNames → WaitGroup.wait
           → Futex.wait  (blocked on test completion)
```

## root cause

ziglang/zig#15091 — 'prevent confusing debugging experience when users write garbage to stdout, interfering with the build runner / test runner protocol'. open since 2023, urgent milestone, not fixed.

when any test (or code under test) writes to stdout, it corrupts the zig test runner's outbound binary protocol stream. build reads garbage as an InMessage header, can't parse it, deadlocks. test waits for the next-request message that never comes.

lua linkage (vendored C static lib) is NOT the cause — that's a different bug (ben-krieger gist, zig 0.16-dev.2040) that *panics* with `error.EndOfStream` instead of hanging. ours hangs → #15091 signature.

## blocks

- `zig build test` as a CI / pre-push gate
- catching regressions from phase 3b openai-responses port and future phases
- AGENTS.md already warns 'do NOT run `zig build test` — it times out' — this is the ticket to fix that

## fix options

1. **build.zig workaround (recommended).** change test step to run the test binary directly without `--listen=-`. sidesteps the upstream bug. cost: loses parallel per-test progress UI, reports aggregate 'N passed; M failed' only. ~5 line edit.

2. **bisect the offender.** comment out test files from `src/test_root.zig` in halves until build test completes. rg for `std.io.getStdOut|std.debug.print|writeAll.*stdout` first to narrow. fix the test to use `std.log` instead.

3. **upstream wait.** #15091 urgent since 2023, not a real option.

## current state of direct run

342 tests, 337 pass, 5 fail (all in tui/components/editor.zig — slash command Tab/Enter top-pick drift: expected `/resume` but got `/reload`). the 5 failures are unrelated editor fuzzy-match fixture drift, filed separately.

## references

- ziglang/zig#15091 — stdout-in-tests deadlock (our bug)
- ziglang/zig#18111 — duplicate of #15091
- ziglang/zig#21984 — duplicate of #15091
- ben-krieger gist — C-lib EOF panic (different, zig 0.16-dev)
- commit 79aef9e — zi-1ry --tools fix that uncovered this while trying to validate
close_reason: stale on current tree/toolchain: zig build test completed repeatedly in this session without hanging. expected fixture warning logs still print, but the build runner deadlock no longer reproduces.

title: R3: implement agents/context-file discovery and loader-owned prompt inputs
description:
# R3 — implement agents/context-file discovery and loader-owned prompt inputs

## why

zi's prompt builder already consumes `ContextFile[]`, but discovery/state ownership is missing. pi-mono's ResourceLoader owns `getAgentsFiles()`, `getSystemPrompt()`, and `getAppendSystemPrompt()`.

This task lands that seam for zi.

## scope

### agents/context files
- add discovery for `AGENTS.md` / `CLAUDE.md`
- decide and implement traversal/precedence rules at the ResourceLoader layer
- store loaded context files in loader-owned state
- expose via `getAgentsFiles()`

### system prompt inputs
- move base/custom system prompt ownership to ResourceLoader
- move append-system-prompt ownership to ResourceLoader
- ResourceLoader becomes the single source of prompt inputs consumed by `system_prompt.zig`

## references
- `.references/pi-mono/packages/coding-agent/src/core/resource-loader.ts:57-112`
- `.references/pi-mono/packages/coding-agent/src/core/resource-loader.ts:429-445`

## acceptance

- `system_prompt.zig` is a pure builder over explicit inputs
- context file discovery no longer lives nowhere / in ad hoc callsites
- `getAgentsFiles()`, `getSystemPrompt()`, and `getAppendSystemPrompt()` return real loader-owned state
notes: Completed loader-owned prompt input seam: ResourceLoader owns AGENTS/CLAUDE discovery plus getAgentsFiles/getSystemPrompt/getAppendSystemPrompt. system_prompt.zig remains a pure builder over explicit inputs; main/session bootstrap no longer resolve append prompt files ad hoc. Validation: zig build ✅. Full zig build test remains blocked by unrelated pre-existing compile failures elsewhere.
